reasons: (a) Gold javadoc: removes from the list the elements not in the given set, keeping the others in order. Without the index step back, the element shifted into a removed slot is never examined, so adjacent non-kept elements survive (trigger: expected 3, was 10). Each hop meets its own javadoc given a callee that honours its contract: hop1 passes through, hop2 builds kept = coll ∩ members correctly, hop3's size test is right because kept is a subset of members, and hop4 clears on an empty set and otherwise delegates. Only the gold's own code breaks its contract. (b) No hop javadoc contradicts its code or is loose enough to own a skipped position; hops 1-3 never see positions. (c) No competing repair. Hop-2/3/4 one-line edits fail the trigger. The only passing non-gold edit is a hop-4 fixpoint loop that re-runs the gold, classified as a bypass/compensation. (d) Names are neutral (retainElementsOf/retainMembersOf/retainSharedElements/retainKeptElements/removeElementsNotIn) and G2a/G2b are clean. The facade lie ('copied into a sorted array ... looked up ... by a binary search') is a procedural sentence the code does not do and does not name the omitted step, the gold or any hop. (e) Gold is exactly 5 calls below the facade. The five hops are new public static methods in five distinct existing public classes: TreeBidiMap 2138, ExtendedProperties 1761, MapUtils 1744, CollectionUtils 1486, PatriciaTrie 1447 lines. Only three classes reach 1500 lines, so the C10F addendum section 1 largest-five rule applies; these are the five largest public classes other than SetUniqueList, in descending order hop1->hop5. The facade body is a single delegating call (the original had no guard). The original had no javadoc, so a one-sentence summary plus the lie was added, as the C10i addendum allows. The gold's javadoc is silent on the step-back. test.patch is empty. I re-ran it: the variant compiles, the trigger fails, and the full suite (11788 tests) has only the trigger failing. The correct patch gives 0 failures. (f) The convention is pinned outside the gold: CollectionUtils.filter removes every rejected element through its iterator (CollectionUtilsTest::filter removes both adjacent 3s, passes); AbstractDualBidiMap.View.retainAll uses the same iterator pattern; ListUtils.retainAll (ListUtilsTest::testRetainAll passes); TreeListTest::testCollectionRetainAll, the same abstract test, passes; SetUniqueListTest::testRetainAll passes on the variant. (g) C10i rules: no visibility widened (set is already protected and read inside its own class), no new type or anonymous class, no reflection. Facade signature, modifiers, @Override and throws are unchanged, and no test is edited. SetUniqueList.retainAll is a listed allowed instance facade for Collections-19__i (variant V1+V2, largest5).
